title: Test double-registers device; double-unregisters on cleanup
description: Trigger: wc_crypto2dev_test() calls wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice(WOLF_CRYPTO2DEV_DEVID, ...) directly, then test_tls13_integration() calls wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid(ctx), which calls RegisterDevice again on the same DEVID and sets g_devid_registered=1. At done:, the test calls wc_CryptoCb_UnRegisterDevice once, then wc_crypto2dev_cleanup() calls it again because g_devid_registered=1. Bad behavior: (1) if wolfSSL rejects double-registration with an error, test_tls13_integration fails spuriously. (2) double-unregister at test end — benign if wolfSSL is idempotent but represents broken state tracking. The test should either not call RegisterDevice directly (let assign_devid do it) or reset g_devid_registered=0 after the manual registration so cleanup does not double-unregister.
notes: RegisterDevice silently overwrites on duplicate devId (confirmed in cryptocb.c:444-453). UnRegisterDevice on an already-removed devId is a silent no-op (returns void, GetDevice returns NULL). So: the double-registration causes no error and no behavioral difference (same callback). The double-unregister at done: is also harmless — second call is a no-op. Not a real failure mode, just messy state tracking in the test. Downgraded from P0.
